overall_assessment: Reviewed all 19 packet entries (7 suspects and 12 random controls): top-level splitting and the displayed learning-outcome groups are generally intact, but substantive allocation errors remain in mixed blocks, including controls. The MG1NA3/UHULV bibliography leaks, 050-E11 internal coursework-label leaks, IA4212 teaching-method leak, V-RETT8200 reading-list blob and KH-EMNE2 empty flag are false alarms; the MAR4020 reading-list leak cannot be resolved because its triggering passage is outside the displayed excerpt. Unflagged defects include misplaced compulsory work, a split assignment description, administrative prerequisites and notices, and recurring library headers; packet display caps were not treated as extractor truncation.

findings.evidence: Registrering av nærvær er obligatorisk og et arbeidskrav i kliniske studier.
findings.description: Mixed source blocks are retained under their headings instead of being allocated by meaning. In 050-E11, teaching_methods contains mandatory attendance, absence limits and attendance documentation, which belong in coursework_requirements, and the final clinical pass/fail judgement, which belongs in assessment. NETPRL likewise repeats the four compulsory submission tasks in teaching_methods despite identifying them as exam gates in coursework_requirements. Conversely, 15DIGRAF files a complete paragraph about ongoing informal supervision and formative feedback under coursework_requirements although it describes teaching rather than an approval requirement. These are unflagged semantic errors; the flagged internal references to learning outcomes and activities within 050-E11 coursework are legitimate descriptions of the requirements.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: R/section_heading_map.R maps Praksis and learning-activity headings to teaching_methods, and sectionize() in R/extract_sections.R keeps their whole blocks there. Although USN enables section_inline_coursework, .split_inline_coursework() only examines assessment, so it cannot correct compulsory work in teaching_methods or teaching prose in coursework_requirements.
findings.suggested_fix: Add narrowly scoped USN routing inside mixed blocks: move complete mandatory-attendance, absence and required-documentation statements from teaching_methods to coursework_requirements; move explicit final clinical grading statements to assessment. Move the standalone formative-supervision paragraph in coursework_requirements to teaching_methods. Retain genuine practice and supervision descriptions, and keep graded assessment components separate from approval gates.

findings.evidence: Teksten skal vere på nynorsk, og blir vurdert til bestått/ ikkje bestått.
findings.description: In this random control, coursework_requirements contains the written assignment that must be approved before the exam, but assessment retains its dependent sentence specifying Nynorsk and pass/fail judgement. The actual final assessment is separately described as an individual written exam in either language form, graded A-F. The compulsory assignment is therefore split between two canonical sections, making coursework incomplete and implying an additional final assessment.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: R/extract_sections.R::.split_inline_coursework() moves sentences recognized by .gate_sentence_regex individually. A following sentence beginning Teksten does not itself state an exam gate, so its language and approval conditions remain in assessment after the antecedent has moved.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend USN inline-coursework routing to carry dependent follow-up sentences about the same assignment, including language and approval scale, until an explicit final-assessment lead such as Sluttvurderinga or a new exam component. Do not move every pass/fail sentence: final graded assessments can also use that scale.

findings.evidence:
Realkompetanse kan vurderes.
Forkunnskap fra andre emner er ikke nødvendig.
findings.description: Prerequisites cleanup leaves non-subject-matter entry administration. IA4212 emits only Generelle opptakskrav.; NETPRL emits an admission-by-experience notice and an explicit statement that no prior courses are necessary, so neither course has a substantive prerequisite to extract. NMARB30 correctly retains the 60-credit requirement but also retains application timing and the placement-contract sentence. The MAKM219 control similarly retains a separate English sentence pointing to programme admission rules after its genuine prior-course requirement. These unflagged errors coexist with correctly suppressed admission-only text in 15DIGRAF; KH-EMNE2's flagged Bestått emne 1 is a valid prerequisite.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: R/extract_sections.R::.strip_admission_lines() lacks coverage for Generelle opptakskrav, Realkompetanse kan vurderes, Det søkes om opptak and English admission pointers. The placeholder patterns do not cover Forkunnskap fra andre emner er ikke nødvendig, while placement-contract administration is not removed by either cleanup.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend sentence-level prerequisite cleanup with anchored Norwegian and English admission-pointer patterns, placement-application/contract sentences, and explicit no-prior-knowledge phrases; drop rows that then contain no substantive requirement. Preserve the genuine prior-course, credit and subject-background conditions, including whole sentences that combine admission wording with a real academic prerequisite.

findings.evidence: Det tas forbehold om mindre justeringer i planen.
findings.description: Text belonging to no canonical section survives in controls. Assessment in 15DIGRAF includes the plan-change reservation and generic regulation pointers; NORVU103 assessment similarly ends with Det kan bli mindre endringar i planen. NETPRL teaching_methods retains the standalone total-workload sentence Det forventes en arbeidsinnsats på ca 200 timer. These are plan administration or workload, rather than assessment design or teaching methods, and course_plan_spec.md places them outside the seven sections. Permitted aids and exam durations elsewhere in the packet are valid assessment design and were not treated as logistics.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: R/extract_sections.R::.clean_sections() keeps running text under mapped headings unless a cleanup pattern removes it. The USN .section_noise entry only targets the detailed fitness-to-practise notice, and .logistics_sentences has no USN entry for these non-sectional sentences.
findings.suggested_fix: Add narrowly anchored USN section-cleanup rules for generic plan-change reservations, bare regulation cross-references with no assessment rule, and standalone total-workload statements. Remove them only from section output, retaining them in the full plan; preserve concrete assessment rules, teaching arrangements and contact-time descriptions.

findings.description: All 12 displayed substantive reading lists retain library identity headers containing a course title/code, usually with campus metadata. Fysikk 0 also retains LREAL Kull, and NORVU103 retains a semester-bearing list identity line. These are course/catalogue labels rather than references or syllabus instructions. This is minor recurring noise, independent of list length and of bibliographic titles that legitimately contain teaching or learning-outcome terminology. Where different campuses have different assigned books, the campus grouping itself conveys useful syllabus context and should be preserved.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: R/extract_sections.R::.strip_list_tabs() removes only leading identity labels that repeat later. The per-list title/code headers remain, as do standalone cohort labels and headers following introductory syllabus prose.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend USN reading-list cleanup to remove redundant course-title/code identity text and standalone cohort/semester metadata, matching against the current course identity. Handle headers after introductory notes as well as leading headers, and retain campus group labels when needed to associate references with the correct campus. Preserve bibliography entries, topical groupings and assigned-reading instructions.
